question.text: Mara has a child not a year old. Bring Mara home unhurt every dawn.

chronicle.text: The other 84 nights of winter went by routine, the wall stood in turns. Yunus and Tamar stood the most of them.
The thaw brought down the east wall where it was climbed all winter. It cannot be stood next winter.
Teo and Zehra came up the valley with their child Jonas, fleeing a raid, and asked to stay. They live behind the mill wall.
A thin harvest: the granary is half empty going into winter.
The autumn fair came to the meadow below the Gate.
Masons from the fair raised the east wall again before the snow.
You named Mara heir to the Gate, before Tamar had said a word.
Mara and Joss are expecting a child.
Winter came. Strangers were seen at the autumn fair. Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.
Not done: Bring every soul and the granary to the thaw.
The rest of the winter, 82 nights, passed in turns on the wall: cold, dark and uneventful. Ruslan and Joss took the most turns.
Rebuilt by the masons, the east wall was still climbed 13 times this winter.
Mara, named heir at the fair, never stood the Gate this winter. The Gate is learned on the Gate.
Ruslan went down the valley in the hungry spring, to kin who could feed them. Their house stands empty.
Ruslan left: the first household to go.
A hungry spring: the granary could not reach the harvest, and one household went down the valley. Yunus gave away half of every bowl and grew thin.
Mara and Joss had a son, Umut.
Kian took sling lessons from Tamar in the summer evenings.
A good harvest, but the granary is half empty going into winter.
The autumn fair came to the meadow below the Gate.
A bigger bell was hung over the Gate.
Seed grain was bought for next year.
Winter came. A hard frost has driven the packs down early. Mara has a child not a year old. Bring Mara home unhurt every dawn.

alerts.text: The bell rings out from the Gate and carries the length of the wall. You call Mara by name: hold your post! “Holding!” Mara calls back.
Mara drove a thief off the west wall.
Movement in the dark on the gate road.
Kian says the Gate will have to wait. “I can’t keep my eyes open.”
Tamar calls from the Gate: “Kian’s gone home to bed.”
Something at the foot of the gate.
A cry from the Gate: someone is down.
Grain is gone: something got over the gate.
Mara nods off at the west wall.
